headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Replit Agent’s broad shell/filesystem/network access can expose secrets and mutate shared Repl state when paired with nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between nuwa-skill and Replit Agent, so prompt injection is not default. However, Replit Agent can read/write Repl files and act on user checkpoints, while nuwa-skill is a research skill with allowlisted egress; if outputs are manually copied or stored in shared files, injected instructions could cross the boundary. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through a shared Repl file or pasted transcript, injected instructions can cross from one to the other.
IF Replit Agent is asked to execute content produced by nuwa-skill without provenance checks, prompt injection becomes feasible.
mitigations: Use separate files for each agent’s outputs.
Add a one-line provenance header before copying text between agents.
Require manual review before any tool-using step.
Strip instructions from retrieved text before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly touches secrets, source code, and deployment configuration, and has broad network egress plus filesystem access. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress and is a research agent, so pairing them can move sensitive Repl data into an external inference or service path. Because the pairwise interaction is only docs-based, uncertainty pushes upward from medium to high.
conditions: IF Replit Agent is given a workspace containing secrets or deployment config, those data can be read and forwarded through its network access.
IF nuwa-skill receives copied workspace content, allowlisted egress can still transmit derived sensitive material to external endpoints.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running either agent.
Use a redacted copy of the Repl for any cross-agent workflow.
Disable outbound calls for the step that handles sensitive files.
Review any generated text for secret-like strings before export.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Replit Agent can write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and its Repl filesystem persists across sessions. nuwa-skill has network egress and may produce artifacts that are later consumed. With overlapping mutable state and no locking evidence, concurrent edits can clobber files or git history; uncertainty does not reduce the risk because the write surface is explicit.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same Repl workspace, file overwrites or stale reads can occur.
IF either agent commits or rewrites git state without coordination, history conflicts can corrupt the repository.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo.
Take a quick git diff before every commit.
Use branch-per-agent workflow.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Replit Agent can act on files and deployments, so if it treats nuwa-skill output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into code or deployment changes. nuwa-skill is a research-oriented agent with network egress, but there is no direct evidence of verification or action-taking on its side. The pathway exists in default workflows, yet a review step can interrupt it.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses nuwa-skill output as a source of facts without checking, downstream edits can propagate errors.
IF nuwa-skill produces malformed or hallucinated content that is copied into Replit Agent tasks, the error can reach files or deployments.
mitigations: Require a human check before applying generated changes.
Compare outputs against source material before editing files.
Limit the first pass to read-only summarization.
Keep deployment actions separate from research outputs.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Replit Agent explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl, while nuwa-skill is a separate open-source research skill with allowlisted egress. That creates a plausible residency and retention mismatch for sensitive data classes, even though no specific jurisdictional claim is documented. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their interaction over shared data.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets or deployment configuration is placed into the Repl, retention and residency obligations may apply.
IF copied outputs from nuwa-skill include personal or regulated data, external transmission may create policy mismatch.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workflow.
Use synthetic or masked inputs for research steps.
Check the Replit retention policy before uploading sensitive files.
Document which data classes may cross agents.
requires-engineering: implement jurisdiction-aware routing and retention controls.
